Each strategy was tuned and selected on validation data by the same rule, and every comparison was repeated across 10 seeds with Friedman and Holm-corrected tests. SCAFFOLD ranked first in both federations (AUC-ROC 0.886 and 0.819) and in 17 of 18 variants, but its margin over the runner-up never exceeded 0.008, and a control sharing its local optimizer attributed most of its margin over FedAvg to drift correction. On the multi-hospital federation, federated training matched centralized training. In the care-unit federation, three protocol choices changed discrimination by more than the choice of strategy did: discharge-coded predictors (+0.038 in AUC-ROC), client-level SMOTE (up to -0.074), and evaluating the last instead of the best validation round (up to -0.084). Platt scaling on validation data repaired the risks distorted by imbalance corrections without loss of discrimination. Studies should therefore fix the protocol before ranking algorithms.

classification.tldr: 在医院联邦学习死亡率预测任务中发现评测协议选择对结果的影响超过聚合算法选择，强调应先固定协议再比较算法。

papers.title: Protocol Choices Matter More Than the Aggregation Algorithm: Federated Learning for In-Hospital Mortality Prediction in Care-Unit and Multi-Hospital Federations

papers.abstractEn: The original EneMonIE proposal describes a Web-based semantic system for continuously monitoring energy trends through targeted information extraction from heterogeneous online media. This article presents EneMonIE-Backend, an implementation-derived redesign that converts that conceptual pipeline into a modular, executable, and application-independent backend. The architecture separates five concerns: data sources, acquisition and normalization, semantic processing, knowledge organization, and persistent storage. It operationalizes configurable connectors for RSS feeds, URL collections, arXiv, social-media JSON files, and open-data CSV files; it also introduces question-driven Web search and scraping. Relevant documents pass through energy categorization, named entity recognition, temporal and event extraction, source sensitive sentiment analysis, and extractive summarization. The resulting semantic representations support entity co-occurrence graphs, cross-document interlinking, cluster-level information fusion, and relational persistence in SQLite. Three grounded question-answering paths are exposed at the backend level: live Web evidence, the stored corpus, and selected configured resources. Answer generation uses a language model when configured and otherwise falls back to deterministic extractive output. Unlike the original proposal, the presented architecture deliberately excludes the user-interface and server-side application layers, allowing the semantic core to be embedded in different applications. A deterministic smoke validation confirms relevance filtering, persistence, clustering, evidence retrieval, and document deletion. The work provides a reproducible architectural basis for future evaluation on larger multilingual energy corpora.

classification.tldr: 该文将能源领域信息抽取概念系统重构为模块化可执行后端，集成数据采集、实体与事件抽取、语义组织和基于证据的问答路径，并提供确定性验证。

papers.title: From Conceptual EneMonIE to an Executable Backend: A Modular Architecture for Energy Information Extractionand Grounded Question Answering

papers.abstractEn: We propose AutoMARS (Automatic Multi-Agent Risk Assessment), an agentic framework for automatic and scalable comparative risk assessment in supply chain networks. The framework enables end-to-end execution of analytical workflows by automatically planning tasks, coordinating specialized agents, invoking external analytical tools, and synthesizing domain-specific results into integrated risk evaluations. AutoMARS further supports scalable risk comparison across multiple locations by parallelizing independent analytical tasks. The framework adopts a multi-domain, multi-agent, and multi-tool architecture that integrates heterogeneous risk factors from socioeconomic, disaster, environmental, and transportation domains. Through coordinated agent interactions and tool integration, AutoMARS enables structured, systematic, and interpretable comparative analysis to support supply chain risk-aware location evaluation.

classification.tldr: 提出一个面向供应链风险评估的多智能体框架，通过自动任务规划、专业智能体协作与外部工具调用实现端到端、可并行的可扩展风险比较分析。

papers.title: AutoMARS: Automatic and Scalable Multi-Agent Large Language Model Framework for Supply Chain Risk Assessment

papers.abstractEn: The relationship between odor chemistry and perception remains incompletely understood. Many existing studies focus on the perception of single molecules, whereas natural odors contain tens to hundreds of components, adding extra layer of complexity to percept formation. Here, we explore the relationship between molecular composition and perceived similarity in natural odor objects. We study this using a database of more than 1,200 volatile-compound-in-food mixtures containing more than 8,000 molecular components, and use large language models (LLMs) as a scalable surrogate for deriving mixture-level perceptual descriptions. We find that language-derived representations provide useful supervision for predicting held-out mixture similarities from molecular composition. The prediction was consistently strongest when perceptual targets were derived from chemosensory prompts than from other sensory prompts. Further, during the mixture-level training, we learned low-rank molecular embeddings that enabled better prediction of held-out mixture similarities than component-overlap metrics, even for mixture pairs with no shared molecules. Although no single-molecule labels were used during training, the learned molecular geometry showed significant alignment with the independent human odor-descriptor space. Finally, we explored the use of external molecular features in our mixture-similarity prediction task. These features showed modest zero-shot alignment with mixture-level perceptual similarity. They improved prediction under limited supervision but offered little additional predictive benefit with the full training set. Together, these results show that language-derived descriptions can provide scalable supervision for predicting the perceptual organization of complex natural mixtures, contributing to a quantitative understanding of how molecular composition gives rise to odor perception.

classification.tldr: 该文利用LLM生成的气味描述作为监督信号，从分子组成预测天然气味混合物的感知相似性，学习到的分子嵌入与人类气味描述空间显著对齐。

papers.title: Learning Perceptual Geometry of Natural Odor Mixtures from LLM-Derived Descriptors

papers.abstractEn: Automated alpha factor discovery is critical for modern quantitative research. While large language models (LLMs) have increasingly been integrated into quantitative workflows, existing agent-based approaches remain highly susceptible to severe backtest overfitting. To address this challenge, we propose EvoQuantLab, a training-free, dual-loop self-evolving framework for robust factor discovery. Instead of relying entirely on LLM generation, EvoQuantLab deploys an inner genetic-programming (GP) loop that dramatically improves token efficiency while evolving typed factor expressions under structural and diversity constraints. An outer diagnosis loop then systematically audits evidence across cycles to drive protocol-level improvements. Furthermore, our evaluation pipeline applies multi-metric validation to rigorously filter out spurious factors before deployment. Extensive out-of-sample experiments across both daily and hourly frequencies -- covering equities and cryptocurrency -- demonstrate the robustness of EvoQuantLab. Specifically, on daily CSI 500 and S&P 500 tasks, EvoQuantLab achieves leading annualized returns of 18.34% and 21.30%, consistently outperforming existing agent baselines. On high-turnover hourly cryptocurrency data, EvoQuantLab delivers a 37.91% annualized return while effectively avoiding execution collapse.

classification.tldr: 该工作提出免训练的双环自进化智能体框架，用内层遗传编程生成因子表达式、外层诊断环审计证据，显著缓解回测过拟合并提升股票与加密货币量化收益。

papers.title: EvoQuantLab: Training-Free Dual-Loop Evolution for Auditable Quantitative Research

papers.abstractEn: On 6 October 2026 OpenAI published an initial 722 AI-written mathematical manuscripts, organized into 372 problem families, in the public repository github.com/openai/math. The release includes claimed solutions to many prominent open problems. We approach this collection as a treasure mine of mathematical ideas. Our aim is to extract new lemmas, constructions, inequalities and proof mechanisms introduced in the source arguments, and to distinguish them from established tools and new combinations of those tools. We call these mathematical instruments. Extraction comes first; their validity, novelty and possible reuse then become subjects for further study. The resulting descriptions also help readers understand the selected papers without having to reconstruct every argument at the outset. We examine 38 families in two groups of 17 and 21, spanning number theory, geometry, analysis, combinatorics, complexity, algebra, operator algebras, topology and mathematical physics. Each entry records the claim, extracted instruments, antecedents and caveats. Eleven cross-cutting patterns connect the entries, and a scoreboard records formalization status and dependencies. Novelty assessments are provisional and sometimes mixed. Selected source comparisons correct mathematical statements, hypotheses and counts; they do not independently establish priority or certify the underlying proofs. No Lean development was compiled or kernel-checked for this survey. We also briefly describe a subsequent application of the signed restriction lemma from family 112 to circuit lower bounds at every fixed depth.

classification.tldr: 对OpenAI发布的AI生成数学文稿进行系统梳理，抽取其中的新数学工具并评估其新颖性与有效性，发现若干跨领域模式。

papers.title: What the Machine Invented: Mining New Mathematical Instruments from OpenAI's October 2026 Release of AI-Generated Mathematics

papers.abstractEn: Most prior work on predicting mental health help-seeking treats it as post-hoc classification of users already active in clinical communities, which cannot tell whether someone approaching a transition can be identified in advance. We instead frame help-seeking as a time-to-event problem and ask which Reddit users will eventually seek mental health support, and how imminent that transition is. We build a two-arm cohort: a control frame of 6,337 ordinary users with genuine right-censoring (12.1% transition rate) to answer who will transition, and a clinical frame of 5,023 eventual transitioners to answer how soon. Features come only from posts written before any clinical activity, and user-grouped five-fold cross-validation plus a four-year temporal holdout guard against leakage. We compare TF-IDF, MentalBERT embeddings and behavioural activity features using Cox proportional hazards models, Random Survival Forests and an LSTM sequential model. Behavioural features alone outperform text for predicting who will seek help (C-index 0.797 vs. 0.763), and combining both is best (0.823 under cross-validation, 0.856 on the holdout). The pattern reverses for predicting how soon a known transition will happen: text remains a stable predictor (C-index 0.698) while behavioural features become unstable. Structural engagement patterns therefore carry information about future help-seeking beyond linguistic content, and separating who from when yields a cleaner analysis.

classification.tldr: 将Reddit用户心理健康求助行为建模为生存分析问题，发现行为特征更能预测谁会求助，而文本特征更能预测何时求助。

papers.title: Predicting Mental Health Help-Seeking Behaviour on Reddit: A Survival Analysis of Linguistic and Behavioural Signals

papers.abstractEn: Artificial Intelligence (AI) models are increasingly developed, published and used across scientific fields. Researchers, students and industry professionals who want to apply these models to their own research questions often lack the programming and data science expertise to do so. Existing guidelines cover single steps, but not the route from a published model to working predictions on one's own data. Here we present the hands-on workflow PRAISE, a Practical, Reproducible AI-model Implementation for Science and Education, that helps non-programmers implement published AI models step by step. Because implementations rarely work the first time, PRAISE anticipates common failures and provides a fallback route for each. As a proof of principle, three BSc chemistry students and their tutor applied PRAISE without prior programming or data science knowledge. They reproduced, validated and extended a state-of-the-art model that predicts enzyme-substrate interactions. This shows that with PRAISE, implementing an AI model from the literature becomes a learnable skill, one that turns non-programmer scientists from users into evaluators and improvers of AI models.

classification.tldr: 提出面向非程序员科学家的可复现AI模型实现工作流，并通过化学本科生复现酶-底物预测模型验证其可行性，使模型实现成为可学习的技能。

papers.title: PRAISE: A Reproducible Workflow for Non-Programmer Scientists to Implement Published AI Models

papers.abstractEn: Drug discovery remains a resource-intensive and time-consuming process, involving billions of dollars and a decade of development to advance a drug to market. While many in silico tools have accelerated this process, operating them still demands substantial time, effort, and expertise from medicinal chemists. Autonomous systems built on Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as a promising solution, yet current designs limit their performance. Existing single-agent systems scale poorly to long-horizon, multi-step, and realistic tasks, whereas multi-agent systems typically execute predefined workflows that cannot capture the iterative, non-linear nature of a real drug discovery campaign. Here, we present MADDIE, a multi-agent drug discovery engine. It comprises a central agent, Orchestrator, and four specialized worker agents: HitIdentifier, LeadOptimizer, Synthesizer, and Evaluator, each representing a critical step in a drug discovery campaign. Under Orchestrator's orchestration and coordination, these worker agents are composed into flexible workflows, enabling MADDIE to adapt its strategy and navigate the drug discovery pipeline end-to-end. Across 50 protein targets, MADDIE produces molecules satisfying key property requirements and their synthesis routes, outperforming existing agentic systems, generative models, and general-purpose LLMs by a wide margin. Our analysis reveals how these agents collaborate and that MADDIE can employ different strategies across targets to achieve the campaign's goal, while still being efficient in time and tokens. Together, they demonstrate MADDIE as a low-cost, effective, and efficient autonomous engine for accelerating drug discovery. Code and dataset is available via https://github.com/ninglab/MADDIE.

classification.tldr: 构建由编排者与四个专业子代理组成的多智能体药物发现引擎，可灵活组合工作流端到端完成从命中识别到评估的流程，在50个蛋白靶点上大幅超越现有系统。

papers.title: MADDIE: Multi-Agent Drug Discovery Engine

papers.abstractEn: Studying event memory requires defining events and their relationships within remembered experience. Autobiographical narratives provide evidence of this organization, but their analytical units must first be established. This study introduces a large language model framework for constructing event representations from narratives and modeling their structure and dynamics with excerpt-level traceability. Explicit boundary rules and a feature schema informed by hippocampal models of episodic memory and navigation guide event construction. In a proof-of-concept application to interviews from five participants, the framework constructed 256 event-states. Multiple correspondence analysis embedded these states in feature-based spaces, with analyses focused on a selected 4-D geometry and 10-D and 13-D reference geometries. Consecutive event-states were significantly closer than expected under randomized narrative order. In the selected 4-D ten-basin solution, similarity between basin-state feature profiles corresponded with similarity between one-step routing profiles; context, mechanism, and theme differentiated full-system pathway engagement. A successor representation modeled expected basin-state occupancy across successive steps. Correlations between basin-centroid distances and complete successor-profile distances were positive across all five basin solutions, with exploratory tests supporting correspondence in at least two solutions across all three geometries. These findings connect feature-based event representations with observed narrative transitions and modeled multistep organization. The framework translates hippocampal principles into source-linked event boundaries and state representations, providing an analytical basis for testing neural accounts of event segmentation and predictive organization during naturalistic recall.

classification.tldr: 提出基于大语言模型的自传体叙事事件表征框架，将海马事件分割原则转化为可溯源的事件边界与状态空间，并验证叙事状态转移的几何组织规律。

papers.title: Event Memory and Narrative Dynamics: A Large Language Model Framework for Multidimensional State Spaces

papers.abstractEn: Inferring tumor-growth laws from sparse, noisy observations requires more than accurate curve fitting. We study an AI-assisted workflow involving symbolic regression, mathematical admissibility checks, coefficient refitting, and large language model (LLM) ranking. Synthetic Gompertz data allow trajectory fit, forecasting, and recovery of the governing growth law to be assessed separately. A dense noiseless control recovers the generating family, but sparse noisy sampling frequently leads to alternative forms. Among retained candidates in the tested configurations, physics-informed neural network refitting often increases growth-law error, whereas classical nonlinear least squares usually reduces it. A separate exploratory analysis of archived LLM rankings shows no consistent improvement over selection by training error and identifies errors in mathematical reasoning. Plausible saturation, accurate trajectory fits, and convincing explanations can therefore coexist with incorrect growth laws. Mathematical validity and law recovery require evaluation alongside predictive performance.

classification.tldr: 针对稀疏噪声数据下的肿瘤增长定律发现，提出符号回归、系数重拟合与LLM排序结合的工作流，发现仅凭拟合优度和LLM排序可能选出错误的增长定律。

papers.title: AI-Assisted Tumor-Growth Law Discovery from Sparse Data: Refitting and LLM-Based Ranking

papers.abstractEn: Symbolic regression (SR) aims to discover interpretable mathematical expressions from data and plays a key role in scientific discovery. However, existing methods face a common bottleneck: the enormous search space and severe combinatorial explosion make it difficult to achieve a favorable trade-off between accuracy and algorithmic efficiency. We argue that, in addition to designing increasingly complex solver-specific SR strategies, an equally promising direction is to equip them with a shareable auxiliary strategy that can provide reliable search guidance. To this end, we propose DASS, a solver-adaptable Dynamic Auxiliary Search Strategy that improves SR by constructing and refining a high-potential auxiliary search subspace. DASS represents the auxiliary search space as a functional subspace spanned by a set of high-potential basis function terms. It estimates term utility through multi-environment evaluation, filters unstable guidance, and updates term potential scores with a Gibbs posterior, thereby calibrating the subspace to provide more reliable guidance for downstream solvers. The high-quality solutions produced by the solver are used to update the set of basis terms. This forms a virtuous closed-loop optimization process: the subspace guides the downstream solver, and the solver feedback reshapes the subspace for subsequent exploration. DASS can be easily integrated with various types of SR solvers. Extensive experiments on LLM-SRBench show that DASS significantly improves the accuracy of original solvers with a manageable increase in runtime.

classification.tldr: 提出一种可适配多种符号回归求解器的动态辅助搜索策略，通过构建并迭代更新高潜力基函数子空间来引导搜索，在LLM-SRBench上显著提升求解精度。

papers.title: DASS: A Solver-Adaptable Dynamic Auxiliary Search Strategy for Symbolic Regression

papers.abstractEn: Recruitment applications span diverse operations, from drafting job descriptions and interpreting queries to organizing profiles, assessing fit, and recommending candidates and jobs. Systematic LLM evaluation therefore requires task coverage that reflects this range of business needs. We introduce EHR-Bench, an open Chinese benchmark comprising twelve tasks across six capability families and five recruitment scenarios. The tasks cover generation, extraction, classification, retrieval, semantic similarity, and reciprocal ranking within one evaluation framework. An internal recruitment dataset guides task definitions, the occupation taxonomy and sampling targets, output requirements, and scoring protocols. Following these specifications, we construct 8,336 task instances from public materials and controlled augmentation, with source-aware expert review and documented provenance. We evaluate twelve LLMs through task-level, capability-level, and aggregate comparisons. Closely ranked models exhibit distinct task strengths, and performance varies across input sources, reference evidence, and candidate pools. Five shared models retain the same observed Overall ordering on a private operational reference, with variation in capability and task correspondence. EHR-Bench provides a reproducible foundation for systematic model assessment, task-specific model selection, and further research on LLMs for recruitment. The project repository is available at https://github.com/EhrBench/EHR-Bench.

classification.tldr: 该论文发布一个中文招聘领域多任务基准，涵盖六大能力族十二个任务共8336个实例，并对十二个大模型进行了任务级和能力级的系统评测。

papers.title: EHR-Bench: A Chinese Multi-Task Benchmark for Recruitment AI

papers.abstractEn: Post-route FPGA timing closure remains expert-dependent and computationally expensive. We present LATCH (LLM-Assisted Timing Closure Harness), a two-layer framework that separates large language model (LLM) orchestration from deterministic FPGA implementation and evaluation. Across sixteen designs and seven LLMs, a single-iteration study compares three agent control granularities - expert-written recipes, direct EDA operations and LLM-constructed procedures - to ask how much control an agent needs per attempt. Functional-pass rates are 98.2%, 71.4% and 17.9%, respectively; yet direct operations give slightly larger 3.4% median Fmax gains when passing, versus 3.2% for recipes. This exposes a trade-off between execution reliability and timing improvement. Informed by this trade-off, a multi-iteration study fixes the action tier at expert recipes to ask how repeated attempts are best organised, comparing a fitted deterministic heuristic with sequential LLM reasoning, branching exploration and knowledge base-guided exploration within 12 checkpoints per run. Branching raises mean maximum-frequency improvement from 10.5% (sequential) to 16.0%, and the knowledge base to 20.3%, improving 15 of 16 designs. Characterisation across 2,421 recipe attempts profiled their gain and validation rates, showing hard-block re-placement gives the largest cumulative mean gain at 41.4MHz.

classification.tldr: 提出 LLM 辅助的 FPGA 后布线时序收敛框架 LATCH，系统比较不同代理控制粒度与迭代策略，显著提升最大频率改进。

papers.title: LATCH: LLM-Assisted Timing Closure Harness for Post-Route FPGA Optimisation

papers.abstractEn: Financial candlestick understanding requires locating visual elements, aligning them across trading dates and panels, and combining observations through numerical and financial reasoning. Answer accuracy alone does not reveal whether predictions are supported by chart evidence. We introduce Code-Interactive Financial Candlestick Reasoning and present Fin-Thinker, a model based on Qwen3.5-9B that generates and executes code to acquire evidence and perform computations. The model uses the returned observations to guide subsequent reasoning. To train these capabilities, we construct FinKLine-32K with 32,184 replay-verified code-observation trajectories collected through teacher-guided student exploration. These include successful solutions with and without error recovery. Our three-stage training framework combines foundational visual-code fine-tuning, financial process supervision of successful reasoning and corrective continuations, and execution-feedback reinforcement learning. For evaluation, we introduce FinKLineBench with 1,200 questions across 138 financial task types to assess answer correctness, code execution, and evidence grounding separately. On FinKLineBench, Fin-Thinker improves strict accuracy by 13.1 and 33.2 percentage points over the best-performing direct-answer baseline among those evaluated and its base model with sandbox access, respectively. Training-stage ablations further show that financial process supervision and execution-feedback reinforcement learning yield successive improvements in both answer accuracy and GPT-5.6-judged grounded accuracy.

classification.tldr: 构建金融K线图理解模型，通过生成并执行代码获取证据进行推理，配合三阶段训练与过程监督，在自建基准上显著提升准确率与证据可溯性。

papers.title: Code-Interactive Visual Reasoning for Financial Candlestick Understanding

papers.abstractEn: Real-time AI captioning now serves audiences at multilingual events, yet computer-assisted interpreting (CAI) tools are still built for interpreters, rarely by them. This article reports an autoethnographic design study in which a professional interpreter with no programming training built a local-first CAI system through expert-led 'vibe coding', co-creating with an LLM architect and a coding agent. Analysis of the complete development dialogues shows how tacit professional knowledge, from segmentation to booth infrastructure, was externalized into design after generic defaults failed in use. In a demanding public scientific event, three mechanisms of in-booth appropriation emerge under a firmly human-led division of labor; telemetry from a first fully instrumented assignment shows a fully local chain sustaining a median translation latency of 0.94 s across 971 utterances. The case is read as lead-user innovation newly enabled by generative AI, with implications for the technological literacy of interpreters and the future of interpreter training.

classification.tldr: 通过自民族志研究展示专业口译员与LLM协同开发本地化计算机辅助口译工具，实现0.94秒中位翻译延迟的实际应用。

papers.title: The interpreter as developer: An autoethnographic design study of building a computer-assisted interpreting tool through human-LLM co-creation

papers.abstractEn: Medication recommendation requires jointly considering diagnoses, comorbidities, longitudinal patient history, and treatment interactions. Although recent retrieval-augmented generation approaches using language models have shown promise for clinical recommendation, most existing systems rely on fixed retrieval pipelines that cannot adapt to diverse clinical retrieval scenarios and may introduce noisy or irrelevant evidence. We propose ARMED, an adaptive clinical RAG framework that dynamically expands retrieval according to retrieval sufficiency and current-admission relevance. ARMED first observes the initial retrieval outcome and selectively performs supplementary or fallback multi-query retrieval when additional evidence is needed. The framework also incorporates a relevance gate that activates only clinically relevant same-patient history and organizes retrieved evidence into structured query-level clinical evidence. Experiments on MIMIC-IV demonstrate that ARMED consistently outperforms previous static retrieval baselines and improves overall medication recommendation quality. By combining locally runnable small language models with adaptive retrieval, ARMED supports medication recommendation without relying on external language model APIs or task-specific fine-tuning.

classification.tldr: 该论文提出一种自适应临床检索增强框架，根据检索充分性动态补充或回退检索并过滤相关病史证据，在MIMIC-IV上显著提升用药推荐质量且无需外部API或微调。

papers.title: ARMED: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Medication Recommendation

papers.abstractEn: Multi-step retrosynthesis planning is often considered solved once a route to purchasable starting materials is found, but such a route should also be practical in real-world chemistry. Recent LLM-based planners formulate this process as sequential decision-making over an AND-OR graph, yet typically expand a single molecule per turn and are optimized for solvability alone, leaving alternative routes uncompared across the multiple objectives that determine practicality before the search budget is committed. We introduce RetroPlanner, an LLM-based planner that jointly compares multiple routes to steer the search toward higher synthesizability, as measured by reaction plausibility, round-trip consistency, and starting-material price. RetroPlanner is trained to reason over chemical evidence: structural progress from the target molecule, bond changes and reaction classes, where candidate routes diverge from one another, and how they rank across multiple objectives. Experiments on multi-step retrosynthesis benchmarks demonstrate that RetroPlanner recovers more alternative routes than prior LLM-based planners while improving synthetic route quality and maintaining a high success rate.

classification.tldr: 提出基于大模型的多路线逆合成规划方法，通过多目标比较引导搜索，在基准上恢复更多替代路线并提升合成路线的实用性。

papers.title: RetroPlanner: Multi-Route Expansion and Multi-Objective Reasoning for LLM-Based Retrosynthesis Planning

papers.abstractEn: Recent advances in instruction-driven time series forecasting highlight a fundamental tension: systems must simultaneously master natural-language instruction following and precise numerical prediction. Current approaches often force a compromise. Large language models (LLMs) can interpret unstructured requests but may be inaccurate when asked to produce forecast values directly, whereas time series foundation models (TSFMs) provide numerical forecasts but typically require structured inputs specifying the target series, context window, and horizon. We present ChronoScribe, which applies semantic-numerical specialization to this workflow. A LoRA-adapted LLM proposes an execution path and context length; deterministic rules resolve the executable configuration. On the specialist path, a frozen TSFM produces quantile trajectories for the task-specified horizon. Deterministic trajectory summaries condition the response, while the LLM neither generates nor revises predicted values. We evaluate a Qwen3.5-9B--Chronos-2 implementation across 23 evaluation dimensions and 30 public datasets against eleven proprietary direct LLMs and three open TSFMs. ChronoScribe has the lowest error on sMAPE, MASE, WAPE, RMSE, and MAE among all evaluated systems, including fixed-context controls. Across these metrics, even the lowest direct-LLM error remains 2.0--2.7 times the corresponding ChronoScribe error. At the system level, ChronoScribe achieves a Task-Level Score (TLS) of 65.5, 10.6 points above the strongest direct-LLM baseline. The results support ChronoScribe's division of labor, in which the LLM handles interpretation, configuration, and communication while the TSFM handles numerical forecasting.

classification.tldr: 提出LLM负责指令解析与配置、冻结时序基础模型负责数值预测的分工式时间序列预测系统，在30个数据集上误差显著低于直接用LLM预测的方案。

papers.title: ChronoScribe: Semantic-Numerical Specialization for Instruction-Driven Time Series Forecasting

papers.abstractEn: Accurate breast cancer risk prediction from screening mammography is essential for improved risk stratification and personalized screening. It can benefit from both temporal breast tissue changes across longitudinal examinations and complementary anatomical information from craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) views. Leveraging longitudinal information requires identifying corresponding tissue regions across examinations, yet most approaches rely on implicit feature alignment without explicitly enforcing spatial consistency. Recent work has demonstrated the benefits of explicit temporal alignment; however, existing methods model each view independently, preventing them from exploiting complementary CC and MLO information. Furthermore, explicit approaches have been limited to a single prior examination. To fill these gaps, we propose (github.com/sot176/FlexLMV-Net), a breast-wise longitudinal multi-view framework that jointly models CC and MLO views across screening examinations while accommodating a variable number of prior examinations. FlexLMV-Net explicitly aligns longitudinal feature maps and integrates complementary views through cross-view temporal fusion and a dual-stream attention block. Evaluated on EMBED and CSAW-CC, FlexLMV-Net consistently outperforms existing approaches across breast density, cancer subtypes, and demographic subgroups, highlighting the benefits of explicit longitudinal alignment, multi-view modeling, and flexible use of available screening history. We further introduce (github.com/sot176/BCRBench), an open-source benchmark that unifies state-of-the-art single- and multi-timepoint breast cancer risk prediction models under standardized preprocessing, training, inference, and evaluation protocols, enabling fair and reproducible comparison of existing methods.

classification.tldr: 该论文提出一种显式纵向对齐的多视角乳腺癌风险预测框架，联合建模CC与MLO视图及可变数量的历史检查，在EMBED和CSAW-CC数据集上优于现有方法，并发布了标准化评测基准。

papers.title: Explicitly Aligned Multi-View Breast Cancer Risk Prediction from Variable-Length Screening Histories

papers.abstractEn: As large language models are increasingly adopted as multi-party communication facilitators, there is a growing demand for agents capable of balancing diverse group dynamics across contexts. However, existing LLM facilitators are often fine-tuned for task-specific objectives; generalized LLM-based facilitation methods that can adapt to different types of tasks and diverse group dynamics are underdeveloped. To address this gap, we present GUIDE (Generalized Unified Intervention for Dynamic Exchanges, a framework for developing generalized LLM-based facilitators across different multi-party contexts. GUIDE evaluates facilitation across both objective task outcomes and subjective metrics, including psychological safety and perceived friction. Within this framework, we study whether LLMs can self-learn generalized facilitation strategy offline to real-time interventions. We first collect multi-party human interactions guided by task-specific expert LLM facilitators (N=432 conversations). We then employ a self-learning method in which an LLM induces an actionable strategic playbook from conversations and iteratively refines it using feedback from an LLM judge aligned with human annotators (N=20), developing a single generalized facilitator that outperforms the three task-specific expert facilitators on held-out conversations 61.4% win rate. Finally, we evaluate these improvements empirically; in a real-time online empirical study, the self-learned generalized facilitator preserves facilitator performance and group productivity, improves speaking comfort and reduces interpersonal friction, while using 24.7% fewer turns and 29.0% fewer words than the expert prompts. These findings provide empirical evidence that LLMs can learn generalizable, task-agnostic social facilitation from task-specific human interactions, on-par with hand-crafted task-specific prompts across diverse group settings.

classification.tldr: 提出通用多方对话主持框架GUIDE，通过离线自学习归纳可执行主持策略手册并经评审反馈迭代精炼，学到优于任务专属主持者的通用促进策略。

papers.title: Learning to GUIDE the Group: Self-Learning LLM Facilitation Across Multi-Party Tasks

papers.abstractEn: Real-world studies (RWS) analyze routinely collected healthcare data, such as electronic health records and insurance claims, to estimate treatment effects, monitor safety, and identify risk factors outside randomized trials. Automating RWS with large language model agents is appealing but brittle: valid analyses depend on dataset-specific clinical semantics, including index dates, follow-up windows, patient/event-level units, and outcome boundaries that are often implicit in observational data. This leads to schema mismatches, temporal errors, inconsistent analytical granularity, and unsupported clinical claims. We present ProCARE, a profile-grounded framework that reformulates RWS automation as constrained compilation. ProCARE converts heterogeneous data profiles into Evidence Contracts specifying available variables, temporal attributes, distributions, and evidentiary limits, and compiles study objectives into RWS-IR, a strongly typed intermediate representation for variables, time relations, analysis units, and statistical tasks. Deterministic validation and localized repair then check and revise generated workflows across schema mapping, cohort construction, variable derivation, analysis, and interpretation. On 36 EHR-based benchmark tasks, ProCARE outperforms strong LLM-agent baselines in code executability, semantic consistency, and conclusion traceability, with automated violation diagnoses showing moderate-to-substantial agreement with blinded expert review.

classification.tldr: 提出一种基于数据画像与证据契约的约束式编译框架，将真实世界研究自动化转化为强类型中间表示并确定性校验，显著提升生成工作流的可执行性与结论可追溯性。

papers.title: ProCARE: Real-World Study Automation via Profile-Grounded Evidence Contracts

papers.abstractEn: Transportation planning has traditionally required substantial expertise in network modeling, traffic assignment, and optimization. As a result, strategic analyses such as network design, capacity expansion, and model calibration remain inaccessible to non-expert decision makers. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) provide an opportunity to bridge this gap by enabling natural-language interaction with complex transportation planning tools. However, existing LLM-based systems primarily serve as interfaces to simulation software and lack the ability to efficiently search, evaluate, and optimize transportation solutions. This study proposes an integrated human-AI transportation planning framework that combines a large language model, a model context protocol (MCP) interface, an open-source transportation planning engine (AequilibraE), and a differentiable user equilibrium (UE) assignment layer. The framework allows non-expert users to execute network analyses and improve solutions for optimization. A differentiable UE layer is developed by directly differentiating the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions of the Beckmann traffic assignment problem. The proposed framework is demonstrated through two representative planning tasks: calibration of travel time functions from observed traffic counts and network design under budget constraints. The examples illustrate how differentiable transportation models and LLM agents can jointly democratize transportation planning and substantially reduce barriers between domain expertise and transportation decision making.

classification.tldr: 该工作将大语言模型与可微用户均衡交通分配层结合，构建人机协作的交通规划框架，使非专家用户能通过自然语言完成网络校准与预算约束下的网络设计优化。

papers.title: Large Language Model Assisted Transportation Planning through a Differentiable User Equilibrium Layer

papers.abstractEn: Financial forecasting has traditionally relied on numerical time-series (TS) signals, while textual information such as news remains largely underutilized. We introduce XForecast, a benchmark and competition for news-grounded financial forecasting, where the task is to predict stock price movements four weeks ahead using both historical price data and paired news signals. XForecast combines stock price data with curated financial text generated using FinTexTS, a multimodal dataset generation method. It covers 100 large-cap stocks from 2019--2023, with training on 2019--2022 and evaluation on 2023. To better evaluate models that leverage textual signals, we adopt a weighted hit rate metric that places greater emphasis on instances where news information is expected to have stronger influence. The XForecast Challenge, hosted on Kaggle as part of KDD 2026 Finance Day, aims to benchmark methods for integrating financial TS and textual information.

classification.tldr: 发布结合历史股价与新闻文本的四周股价涨跌预测基准及竞赛，采用强调新闻影响更大的加权命中率指标以评测文本与时序信号融合方法。

papers.title: XForecast: The KDD 2026 Finance Day Challenge on News-Grounded Financial Forecasting

papers.abstractEn: Maintaining up-to-date clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) is essential for evidence-based medicine, but rapid evidence growth and complex expert consensus formation limit timely updates. We developed GUIDE, a multi-agent copilot system for human-AI collaborative guideline generation and updating. GUIDE delegates labor-intensive tasks to specialized AI agents while preserving expert judgment and final arbitration. In 12 NICE ophthalmology datasets, GUIDE achieved 88.85% literature recall, 86.06% alignment in certainty-of-evidence ratings, and 91.67% recommendation agreement, requiring 162.17 minutes per dataset on average (28.68% human intervention). Performance remained stable across 20 additional datasets from cardiology, endocrinology, gastroenterology, and respiratory medicine. Ablation analysis showed that removing expert intervention reduced performance in judgment-intensive steps such as Risk-of-Bias assessment. In six post-cutoff datasets, GUIDE maintained robust end-to-end performance on unseen evidence. Prospective real-world validation showed that GUIDE reduced expert workload and produced more clinically acceptable recommendations than the original decade-old guideline (mean score, 3.73 vs. 1.53; agreement, 66.7% vs. 13.3%), with outcomes comparable to human-only updating (P = 0.588) but substantially less time and effort. GUIDE offers a practical framework for timely, trustworthy, expert-centric guideline development and validates computationally augmented consensus.

classification.tldr: 该论文提出一个多智能体人机协作系统，用于临床实践指南的自动化生成与更新，在眼科等多科室数据集上实现高召回率与推荐一致性，并显著降低专家工作量。

papers.title: GUIDE: Computationally Augmented Consensus for Trustworthy Clinical Practice Guidelines

papers.abstractEn: Personality assessment from asynchronous video interviews (AVIs) plays a crucial role in recruitment by enabling standardized and behaviorally grounded evaluation for job applicants. However, most of the previous works are confined to a single interview protocol. Independently collected protocols differ in question sets and question-trait mapping. Thus, the human-rated evidence from one protocol cannot be used directly under another. To address this limitation, we propose the Cross-protocol Evidence-grounded Personality Assessment (CEPA) framework, which aligns behavioral representations across interview protocols. CEPA addresses protocol heterogeneity by projecting source behavioral records into the target protocol's construct-oriented representation space. It retrieves behaviorally relevant and personality-complementary human-rated exemplars to ground an ensemble of LLM raters, which enables behavior-to-personality associations without target-specific supervision. In cross-protocol experiments, CEPA reduces average mean squared error (MSE) by 43.8% (Forward) and 17.0% (Reverse) relative to the strongest baseline. Our empirical experiments show that human-rated evidence from one protocol can support personality assessment under another without target-specific supervision or retraining.

classification.tldr: 提出跨协议证据锚定的人格评估框架，将不同面试协议的行为表征对齐并借助人类评分样本引导LLM评分，无需目标协议监督即显著降低评估误差。

papers.title: Cross-Protocol Personality Assessment with LLMs: Aligning Behavioral Evidence with Human Ratings
